## Breast Screening

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Breast screening participation, by year
# Data from Victorian Cancer Screening Framework
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in VCSF data
breast_year <- f_read_vcsf("Breast Cancer Screening Participation (2015 - 2023) - with cell-suppression.xlsx",
                           data_sheet    = "8.1 Indigenous - target age",
                           skip_rows     = 6,
                           row_select    = c(2:3),
                           column_select = c(indigenous_status = "x1",
                                             screened_n_2021 = "x2021_2023",
                                             eligible_n_2021 = "x4",
                                             screened_n_2020 = "x2020_2022",
                                             eligible_n_2020 = "x8",
                                             screened_n_2019 = "x2019_2021",
                                             eligible_n_2019 = "x12",
                                             screened_n_2018 = "x2018_2020",
                                             eligible_n_2018 = "x16",
                                             screened_n_2017 = "x2017_2019",
                                             eligible_n_2017 = "x20",
                                             screened_n_2016 = "x2016_2018",
                                             eligible_n_2016 = "x24",
                                             screened_n_2015 = "x2015_2017",
                                             eligible_n_2015 = "x28")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(indigenous_status = dplyr::case_when(
    indigenous_status == "Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander"                                   ~ "aboriginal",
    indigenous_status == "Not Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander/Not stated/Inadequately described" ~ "non_aboriginal",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
breast_year <- breast_year %>%
  f_wrangle_vcsf() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(period = dplyr::recode(period,
                                       "2021" = "2021-2023",
                                       "2020" = "2020-2022",
                                       "2019" = "2019-2021",
                                       "2018" = "2018-2020",
                                       "2017" = "2017-2019",
                                       "2016" = "2016-2018",
                                       "2015" = "2015-2017")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(period)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Breast screening participation, by age group
# Data from AIHW Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Performance Framework
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in AIHW data
breast_age <- f_read_hpf("304-Early-detection.xlsx",
                         data_sheet    = "D3.04.9",
                         skip_rows     = 1,
                         row_select    = c(3:13, 15:22),
                         column_select = c(age_group = "age_group_years",
                                           prop      = "vic")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(indigenous_status = dplyr::case_when(
    row_number() %in% 1:11  ~ "aboriginal",
    row_number() %in% 12:19 ~ "non_aboriginal",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
breast_age <- breast_age %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    indigenous_label = dplyr::case_when(
      indigenous_status == "aboriginal"     ~ "Aboriginal",
      indigenous_status == "non_aboriginal" ~ "Non-Indigenous",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    #
    indigenous_status = factor(dplyr::case_when(
      indigenous_status == "aboriginal"     ~ "Identified as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander",
      indigenous_status == "non_aboriginal" ~ "Did not identify as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      #
      levels = c("Identified as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander",
                 "Did not identify as Aboriginal\nand/or Torres Strait Islander")),
    #
    age_group = factor(dplyr::case_when(age_group == "40–49" ~ "40-49 yrs",
                                        age_group == "50–59" ~ "50-59 yrs",
                                        age_group == "60–69" ~ "60-69 yrs",
                                        age_group == "70–74" ~ "70-74 yrs",
                                        age_group == "75+"   ~ "75+ yrs",
                                        age_group == "50–74 years (age-standardised rate)(d)" ~ "Total (50-74 yrs)",
                                        TRUE ~ age_group))) %>%
  #
  dplyr::filter(!str_detect(age_group, "rate"))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from [Victorian Cancer Screening Framework](https://acpcc.org.au/services/population-health/) and the [AIHW Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Performance Framework](https://www.indigenoushpf.gov.au/).

- Participation in breast screening for eligible Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander women aged 50-74 years in Victoria increased from 32% in 2015-2017 to 37% in 2021-2023. Participation was lower than for non-Indigenous women at each time period.

- 33% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander women aged 50-74 years living in Victoria participated in breast screening during 2019-2020, compared to 46% of non-Indigenous women.

- Participation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander women in breast screening was highest for the 60-69 year (35%) and 70-74 year (36%) age groups.

::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for Figure 9G-1 and Table 9G-1 were obtained from the [Victorian Cancer Screening Framework (VCSF)](https://acpcc.org.au/services/population-health/), maintained by the Australian Centre for the Prevention of Cervical Cancer (ACPCC).
  - The VCSF collates data from the [National Cancer Screening Register](https://www.ncsr.gov.au/) (cervical and bowel screening) and [BreastScreen Victoria](https://www.breastscreen.org.au/) in order to monitor and improve prevention and early detection of breast, bowel, and cervical cancers in Victoria, particularly among priority communities.
  - Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples were defined based on the recording of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status in the individual datasets that make up the VCSF.
  - Data broken down by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status are not publicly available on the VCSF website but can be requested from the ACPCC.
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- For Figure 9G-1 and Table 9G-1, the participation rate is the number of eligible women (aged 50-74 years) screened by BreastScreen Victoria divided by the total number of eligible women (aged 50-74 years) for each two year time period.
  - The total number of eligible women for each two year period is derived from the [ABS Estimated Residential Population (ERP)](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/population/population-projections-australia/2022-base-2071).

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Data for Figure 9G-2 and Table 9G-2 were obtained from the [AIHW Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Performance Framework](https://www.indigenoushpf.gov.au/), compiled from [BreastScreen Australia](https://www.breastscreen.org.au/).
  - The AIHW Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Performance Framework brings together information from a wide range of national, jurisdictional, and regional data sources to report on determinants of health, health outcomes, and health system performance for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples.
  - BreastScreen Australia is the national free breast cancer screening program.
  - Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander women were defined as those who identified themselves as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander at the time of their breast screening appointment.

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- For Figure 9G-2 and Table 9G-2, the participation rates for each age group are the number of women screened during January 2019 to December 2020 as a percentage of the eligible female population, calculated as the average of the 2019 and 2020 [ABS resident population projections](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/population/population-projections-australia/2022-base-2071) based on the ABS Census 2016.
  - The total rates for the 50-74 years age group were directly age-standardised to the Australian 2001 standard population in 5-year age groups between 50 and 74 years.

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_underidentification`

- For Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander women and people with breasts, screening is recommended every two years from 40-74 years of age. For non-Indigenous women and people with breasts, screening is recommended every two years from 50-74 years of age.

- Breast screening that occurs outside of the BreastScreen Victoria program (e.g. private mammography) will not be captured by these data.

- The COVID-19 pandemic affected the availability of screening services and health seeking behaviours, which may have had an impact on screening participation.
:::

## Cervical Screening

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cervical screening participation, by year
# Data from Victorian Cancer Screening Framework
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in VCSF data
cervical_year <- f_read_vcsf("Cervical Screening Participation (2017-2021) - Cell Suppression Applied.xlsx",
                             data_sheet    = "8. Indigenous - target age",
                             skip_rows     = 10,
                             row_select    = c(1, 5),
                             column_select = c(indigenous_status = "indigenous_status_ever_identified",
                                               screened_n_year2  = "participants_screened_3",
                                               eligible_n_year2  = "eligible_population_4",
                                               screened_n_year3  = "participants_screened_7",
                                               eligible_n_year3  = "eligible_population_8",
                                               screened_n_year5  = "participants_screened_11",
                                               eligible_n_year5  = "eligible_population_12")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(indigenous_status = dplyr::case_when(
    indigenous_status == "Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander"             ~ "aboriginal",
    indigenous_status == "Never indicated Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander" ~ "non_aboriginal",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
cervical_year <- cervical_year %>%
  f_wrangle_vcsf() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    eligible = dplyr::case_when(indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" & period == "year2" ~ 1707332,
                                indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" & period == "year3" ~ 1700010,
                                indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" & period == "year5" ~ 1673274,
                                TRUE ~ eligible),
    #
    period = factor(dplyr::recode(period,
                                  "year2" = "2 years (2020-2021)",
                                  "year3" = "3 years (2019-2021)",
                                  "year5" = "5 years (2017-2021)")),
    #
    prop = screened / eligible * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(period)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from [Victorian Cancer Screening Framework](https://acpcc.org.au/services/population-health/).

- During the five-year period 2017-2021 67% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander women and people with a cervix aged 25-74 years had at least one cervical screening test (human papillomavirus test or cervical cytology), compared to 72% of non-Indigenous women.

`r note_data_vcsf`

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_underidentification`

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Cervical screening coverage is the number of eligible women (aged 25-74 years) who had at least one human papillomavirus test or cervical cytology test for any reason divided by the total number of eligible women (aged 25-74 years) for each time period.
  - The total number of eligible women for each two year period is derived from the [ABS Estimated Resident Population](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/population/population-projections-australia/2022-base-2071), adjusted for the number of women who have had a hysterectomy (hysterectomy fraction).
  - Active participants in the [Compass trial](https://acpcc.org.au/compass/) were excluded.

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- The COVID-19 pandemic affected the availability of screening services and health seeking behaviours, which may have had an impact on screening participation.

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>

## Bowel Screening

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bowel screening participation, by year
# Data from Victorian Cancer Screening Framework
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in VCSF data
bowel_year <- f_read_vcsf("Bowel Cancer Screening Participation (2016-2020) - 2019_20 data from Sep21 RDE - final.xlsx",
                          data_sheet    = "8.1 Indigenous target age",
                          skip_rows     = 7,
                          row_select    = c(1, 5),
                          column_select = c(indigenous_status = "indigenous_status_ever_identified",
                                            screened_n_2018   = "participants_screened_8",
                                            eligible_n_2018   = "persons_invited_9",
                                            screened_n_2017   = "participants_screened_12",
                                            eligible_n_2017   = "persons_invited_13",
                                            screened_n_2016   = "participants_screened_16",
                                            eligible_n_2016   = "persons_invited_17")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(indigenous_status = dplyr::case_when(
    indigenous_status == "Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander"             ~ "aboriginal",
    indigenous_status == "Never indicated Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander" ~ "non_aboriginal",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
bowel_year <- bowel_year %>%
  f_wrangle_vcsf() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    eligible = dplyr::case_when(indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" & period == "2018" ~ 1400917,
                                indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" & period == "2017" ~ 1254842,
                                indigenous_label == "Non-Indigenous" & period == "2016" ~ 1014152,
                                TRUE ~ eligible),
    #
    period = factor(dplyr::recode(period,
                                  "2018" = "2018-2019",
                                  "2017" = "2017-2018",
                                  "2016" = "2016-2017")),
    #
    prop = screened / eligible * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(period)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from [Victorian Cancer Screening Framework](https://acpcc.org.au/services/population-health/).

- Participation in bowel screening increased for invited Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 50-74 years from 23% in 2016-2017 to 37% in 2018-2019. Participation was lower than for non-Indigenous people at each time period.

::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" icon=false collapse=false}
`r note_data_vcsf`

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_underidentification`

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- The participation rate is the number of faecal occult blood test kits (bowel screening kits) returned within 30 months divided by the total number of people aged 50-74 years who were sent an invitation to participate in the bowel screening program for each time period.
  - People aged 50-74 years were sent a faecal occult blood test kit once every two years.
  - The number of people invited to screen was derived from the [ABS Estimated Resident Population](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/population/population-projections-australia/2022-base-2071).

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Bowel cancer screening activities (e.g. colonoscopy) may also occur outside of the scope of the national screening program and this may affect bowel cancer screening participation rates.

- The COVID-19 pandemic affected the availability of screening services and health seeking behaviours, which may have had an impact on screening participation.
:::
